decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete message-176 MODIFY covering straightforward sanitation, removal access, hidden liquid traps, and FOOD_SERVICE scope; no additional propagation is needed.
The candidate already has a message-176 MODIFY specifying the approved food-contact materials, prototype-wide coverage, and FOOD_SERVICE scope.
The candidate already records the message-176 extension of whisk removability into SANITATION and FOOD_SERVICE contexts, while its existing removal attributes remain valid.
The candidate already records the message-176 extension of easy bowl removal into CLEANING, SANITATION, and FOOD_SERVICE contexts.
The existing message-176 MODIFY already broadens isolation from the bottom-bowl seal to all liquids, removes the obsolete narrower key, and adds FOOD_SERVICE scope.
The sanitation and removable-component decision does not change the required pour behavior, texture preservation, flow characteristics, or dispensing sequence.
The sanitation and food-service scope expansion does not alter the barista-facing or downward spout orientation.
Message 176 does not change the solenoid actuation mechanism or button-controlled dispensing behavior.
The prohibition on hidden liquid traps and the sanitation scope expansion do not modify the existing leak-containment requirement.
The candidate already has a complete message-176 MODIFY requiring access for maintenance, servicing, and replacement and extending scope to FOOD_SERVICE.
The candidate already has a message-176 Event covering long-term retention of materials, CAD, wiring, cleaning procedures, and exploded-view documentation.
The request to identify food-contact materials and retain documentation does not reopen or modify the finalized component-selection and BOM deliverable.
